text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Norwegian papers this morning.

- Prime minister Thorbjoern Jagland says China is moving in the right direction although the judicial system needs to be altered. Human rights was the main subject discussed between Jagland and head of China's Peoples' Congress Qiao Shi in Oslo on Thursday.
- Norwegians bought fish worth four billion crowns last year, which is 250 million crowns more than in 1995.

- The Supreme Court said that shareholders in the former UNI Storebrand may sue the former board of directors after their failed attempt to buy up Swedish insurance giant Skandia in 1992. After the failed takeover UNI shareholders lost their investment.

-Private investor Kjell Inge Roekke has enlarged his stake in Storebrand insurer to 10 percent. Roekke's buy up could be an attempt to stop the planned merger between Storebrand and Norway's second largest commercial bank Christiania og Kreditkasse.
-State-owned oil company Statoil has still not decided who to chose as its shipping partner, but it expects a final decision before the summer.

-The number of bankruptcies fell by 30 percent in the first three months of 1997 compared to the same year-ago period. In the first quarter this year 639 bankruptcies were registered against 922 in the 1996 period and 951 in 1995.
